launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-c3
description: Diego's Cloud C3 - the fleet's command-and-control surface as its own APK, lifted out of the SuperApp's C3 section (#648). A five-tab shell drawn by the fleet's bottom-nav island (libs:bottomnav) - Infra, Containers, Home, Ops, Observ (opens on Home), under the fleet's AppTopBar with Configs behind its Settings button - declared in ui.* below and baked through BuildConfig. THE SHELL IS VIEWS AND HOSTS FRAGMENTS, not Compose: the pages this app exists to show are the SuperApp's C3 Fragments, and they are MOVED here rather than reauthored, so the rendering, wording and behaviour are the ones that already shipped. BottomNavIslandView is libs:bottomnav's own documented View-side contract for exactly this case (the SuperApp, cloud-me and cloud-wallet shells use it), so hosting fragments is a first-class path. Topology is the address estate: the SuperApp's c3_public and c3_private cards, one C3HealthFragment scoped two ways over the declared service tables. Observ is Health, the SuperApp's own page:c3/health. Home is the overview. Apps LAUNCHES the three C3 sibling APKs that already exist as their own fleet members through ui.external_apps, the same extapp: idiom the SuperApp used, so nothing is re-implemented; the printed name is DERIVED from each fleet id by dropping the family prefix, because an application has ONE name (#351). Configs holds About. A PAGE IS DECLARED WHEN ITS FRAGMENT EXISTS AND NOT BEFORE: there is no not-built body and no flag that could excuse one, which is what lets test/test-c3-shell.sh assert that every declared page renders real content - the guard whose absence let an empty five-tab APK ship green. The five feed cards, the ntfy centre and the three container dashboards ARRIVED (#648, owner-escalated): the ENTIRE SuperApp c3 section declaration is carried verbatim under ui.sections and its two stacks render as the Topology and Observability pages, with Dagu and the WG mesh as their own pages. The top offset is the MEASURED systemBars u displayCutout inset, read in a non-consuming listener (#407/#477), never a tuned margin. Dark is the default theme (#336, #337). English is the base language (#299). Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

android._doc_application_id: The `c3-` / `cloud-` prefix is a DIRECTORY and fleet-name convention and is deliberately NOT in the applicationId — the ac_c3-watchtower precedent, whose own _doc records why: a wrong package compiles, ships, installs, and leaves a tab that opens nothing. `cloudc3` matches `clouddrive` / `cloudwallet`: the fleet name with its separator dropped.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

modules._doc: Single source of truth for the Gradle module graph. settings.gradle iterates this list.

libs:core._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/ — settings.gradle points projectDir here instead of at a local copy, so a fix lands in every app at build time and copies cannot drift.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE, same as libs:core. Not listed in app.depends_on and not linked in app/build.gradle: libs:core pulls it in with an `api` dependency, which is what gives every app the constellation-wide debug API (127.0.0.1:38090+, own-process logcat) without per-app wiring that would drift.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:updater._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/. Also the reader of the constellation fleet manifest: since #276's fix it falls back to aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json when an app carries no data/ dir of its own, and throws if neither exists — which is why this app needs no data/ dir for the fleet bake.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:perms._doc: #1360 the permission contract (libs:perms): Configs > General > Perms (AppPermsSection, linked by libs:ui-nav-bars), first run (PermsFirstRun), PermsGate, and the state provider helper apps are read through.

libs:theme-background._doc: #1154 shared navigation and theme design, shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:bottomnav._doc_dir: THE fleet bottom-nav island (#565/#579): the five tabs are drawn by the same Compose declaration superapp, mail, wallet, me and drive render — one geometry, one pill, one collapse rule. Shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here. This app reuses the four shared symbols (BottomNavEntry, BottomNavIsland, bottomNavInsets, rememberBottomNavCollapse) and declares its OWN five entries from ui.tabs; it deliberately does NOT reuse bottomnav's `bottomNavItems`, which is cloud-mail's item table and merely lives in that module.

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:ops._doc_dir: Shared BY REFERENCE like every other module here. Carries DaguFragment (the native Dagu DAG list page:c3/dagu opens in the SuperApp) and DaguPrefs, the ONE store of the Authelia bearer the ops routes need. Its build.gradle reads THIS repository's build.json first (consumer-wins) for ui.sections[c3].pages[dagu].dagu_default_server, which is why the verbatim c3 section below is also the lib's config.

libs:ui-kit._doc_dir: 2026-10-15 owner decision: all apps must be Compose. Shared BY REFERENCE: the fleet's Compose kit (CloudKitTheme + KitPalette) that AgentsFragment and CatalogFragment paint with.

libs:ai._doc_dir: The AI panel behind the top bar's AI button: the fleet's AI chat (libs:ai), the SAME shared chat Cloud Code has, over the fleet agent gateway (my-ai-api, mesh only). Shared BY REFERENCE. The gateway's mesh address is baked as BuildConfig.AI_GATEWAY_URL by libs/ai/ai-gateway.gradle, which reads it from this app's data/services_private.json.

libs:model-catalogue._doc_dir: libs:ai's `api` dependency: the shared agent descriptor its Agent picker lists. Listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

ui._doc: EVERY declarative list this app renders. app/build.gradle bakes each into BuildConfig as base64 JSON and Declarations.kt decodes it once; no screen reads a BuildConfig blob itself and no tab id, label or icon name is spelled in Kotlin.
ui._doc_nav: #868 THE ONE navigation declaration (libs:bottomnav's NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island's section ids in display order - Infra | Containers | Home | Ops | Observ, Home deliberately the centre item the way every other fleet five-tab shell places it; ui.sections[] holds each section's id, label, icon and its `pages` (the pill strip PageTabs draws over it); ui.default_section is the one it opens on (Home). Configs is a section that is NOT on the bar: the top bar's Settings > Configs opens it. Order is load-bearing: reordering ui.bottom_nav reorders the bottom nav and nothing else changes, which is the property test/test-c3-shell.sh asserts. The section ids are the ONLY tab ids in the app: C3Shell dispatches on them and the tester diffs that dispatch against the sections in both directions, so a section declared with no screen and a screen with no declared section are both build failures. ui.aliases maps the ids that moved in the 2026-10-16 renames to where they live now.

top_bar._doc: THE first row of the app (libs:bottomnav AppTopBar, declared once for the fleet): a hamburger at the left that opens a side drawer (here: the full tree of every declared section and its pages, tappable), the app's name as the title, and two circular buttons at the right: AI (libs:ai's chat in an anchored panel over the fleet gateway - the same shared chat Cloud Code has) and Settings (a dropdown: Account launches Cloud Account, Configs opens the Configs section). No app draws its own copy of this row (cloud-android-top-bar-guard).

ui._doc_aliases: Ids that MOVED keep working: a deep link (page:c3/<id>, the launcher's shortcut_action), a saved tab or an old tester naming one is rewritten to where it lives now. `sections` maps a renamed section id to its new id (Topology became Containers, Apps became Ops); `pages` maps a moved page id to 'section/page' (the Public and Private URL pages merged into the Table page, which is now the All project's Table, #1454; the Stack page is Infra's). Kotlin reads this map and holds no id literal of its own.
ui._doc_private_sources: #1454 WHERE the owner's PRIVATE data lives, never the content. `identities`: the owner's email identities for Infra > Domains > Public, read at run time from the owner's private repo (the store Cloud Me and Cloud Account read, #1438/#1445) with the owner's GitHub token (typed once, kept encrypted), else a side-loaded or cached copy. The file holds {"emails": [{"address", "label", "provider"}]}. Tests and emulator fixtures use fake emails only.

sections.label: Infra
sections._doc: The fleet's hardware and accounts (owner request, 2026-10-20): four declared rows (#1437, #1471: Bare | APIs | Personal | Domains), each page a page of data/fleet_slice.json - the slice data/gen_fleet_slice.py DERIVES from the fleet's own declarations in cloud-infra (VMs, IPs, buckets, devices, zone records) plus the one new input 1_cloud-configs/src/inputs/fleet-assets.json. Nothing fleet-shaped is typed in this file or in Kotlin (test-c3-infra.sh T3). Containers - the DBs, APIs and MCPs among them - are NOT here: they live in Containers (Topology and Table). The APIs row (#1471) is NOT the fleet's own API containers (those are Containers): it lists the THIRD-PARTY API providers the fleet calls (data/api_providers.json: AI, Scraper), with secret NAMES only.

pages.label: Providers
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment: each provider with account, plan, monthly cost (live from c3-infra-api /cloud/{oci,gcp}/costs, else the declared one) and its console links.

pages.label: VMs
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment: each VM with provider, region, size, public IP, wg0 and wg-public IP. The id is not `vms`: that is a SuperApp sample-stub page id test-c3-full-copy.sh keeps undeclared.

pages.label: Containers-as-Service
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (#1454): the PLATFORMS that run containers, one row each - Google Cloud Run (project, region and service count read from the registry cloudy-t-infra c_vps/vps_gcloud/src/terraform.json cloud_run_services) and any other managed container platform the registry or data/platforms.json container_platforms[] declares. The containers themselves are the Containers page's. Read through data/gen_fleet_slice.py; nothing typed here.

pages.label: Containers-Node-Python
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (#1454): the hosting and runtime PLATFORMS (GitHub Pages, GitHub Actions, Google Firebase, Cloudflare Workers and similar), READ from data/platforms.json hosting_platforms[] and the registry's hosting[] - provider, role. None is typed in Kotlin.

pages.label: Storage
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment: storage HARDWARE and backends only - S3 buckets, Google Drive, each VM's disk (declared size, live usage from /health/tier3/{vm}) and the devices' storage. No DB container (test-c3-infra.sh T2).

pages.label: AI
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (APIs row, #1471): the AI API providers (OpenRouter, Claude) of data/api_providers.json group `ai` - category, console and docs links, the apps and containers that use each, the auth method and the secret NAME only. The group declares this page id; Kotlin spells no provider.

pages.label: Scraper
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (APIs row, #1471): the scraper API providers (Apify, and the self-hosted Cloudy Crawlee as its alternative backend, the shared Apify setting of News, Media and Browser) of data/api_providers.json group `scraper`; secret NAMES only.

pages.label: Desktop
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (Personal row, #1437): the declared PCs (device kinds notebook, desktop) - model, OS, WireGuard IP, role.

pages.label: Mobile
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (Personal row, #1437): the declared phones and tablets - model, OS, WireGuard IP, role.

pages.label: Gadgets
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (Personal row, #1437): every other declared device (smartwatch and any new kind).

pages.label: Control
pages._doc: #1495 NEW CATEGORY (Personal row): the peers-control tool group of cloudy-c3-mcp, the phones' shell, logcat, crashes, apps, wake, call, grant, input, screencap and adb tools (merged from cloudy-android-mcp) plus the phone mesh-endpoint methods. Declared data only: OpsMapFragment over data/ops_maps.json maps.hier_control, generated by data/gen_c3_hierarchy.py from data/c3_hierarchy_map.json.

pages.label: Private
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (Domains row, #1437): the domains the owner bought - diegonmarcos.com registration (Cloudflare registrar and admin, renewal, expiry) and its DNS: web, MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT, CAA/SRV, plus the live zone view from /cloud-data/cloudflare-dns.

pages.label: Public
pages._doc: InfraSectionFragment (Domains row, #1437): the public mailbox domains the owner uses (for example gmail, proton), READ from fleet-assets.json public_domains[], plus (#1454) the owner's email identities, PRIVATE: loaded at run time from the owner's private repo declared in ui.private_sources.identities (never in this repo).

sections.label: Containers
sections._doc: Renamed from Topology (owner request, 2026-10-16). #1454: one top page per PROJECT (All | Cloudy | Cloud-me | CG | Capital | Hardtech | Others), each with a Topology | Table switch (nested pages `<project>_topology`, `<project>_table`; ids are unique per section, the view is the id after the project). Topology = the container dashboards (C3StackFragment over ui.carried_c3.stack_topology) and Table = the sortable, filterable table (RoutesTableFragment), both scoped to the project. Which project a container belongs to is data/container_projects.json (explicit name_overrides, then folder / name prefixes; no match = Others), plus ONE page-wide Filters row above the project strip (All | MCPs | APIs | Apps | DBs | Repos) that filters every block of every project and a group_remap; a project id with no entry there is All. Agents moved to Ops.

sections.label: Ops
sections._doc: #1480 Ops reads Network Mail | Orchestration | Health Observability; each "|" is a declared separator_before, so the sub-groups are [Network, Mail], [Orchestration] and [Health, Observability]. Every top page nests its views (ids `<page>_<view>`, resolved by OpsFragment.leafFragment). Network: WireGuard, Auth and DNS & Caddy are maps of data/ops_maps.json drawn from mesh.json / infra_slice.json / containers_declared.json, then the Network topology tree. Mail: one map. Orchestration: the CI/CD flow map, then the topology views Service, Infrastructure, Declared vs deployed and Release (ui.topology), then Agents (#1454). Health: uptime of every service and the reports. Observability: the logs catcher over c3-infra-api GET /logs/search. Old ids (service, infrastructure, orchestration, network, release, agents) are ui.aliases.pages to their new leaf.

pages.label: Routes
pages._doc: The Network topology view of ui.topology: subnet, VM, Caddy routes, firewall rules.

pages.label: Security
pages._doc: #1495 NEW CATEGORY: the cloudy-c3-api /security/* routes (scan, docker, ssh, tokens, topology, wireguard, secrets) and the sec.* and secrets tools had no page. Data only: OpsMapFragment maps.hier_net_security.

pages.label: Declared
pages._doc: The Orchestration topology view of ui.topology: declared vs deployed.

pages.label: Agents
pages._doc: AgentsFragment (#1454): the launchable C3 siblings. Not a topology view.

pages.label: Tests
pages._doc: #1495 NEW CATEGORY: the /tests/run suites and the obs.debug.test tool. Data only: OpsMapFragment maps.hier_ops_health_tests.

pages.label: Metrics
pages._doc: #1495 NEW CATEGORY: /metrics/* and obs.debug.metrics. Data only: OpsMapFragment maps.hier_obs_metrics.

pages.label: Alerts
pages._doc: #1495 NEW CATEGORY: /alerts/*, /db/alert/* and the obs.db.alert_* tools. Data only: OpsMapFragment maps.hier_obs_alerts.

pages.label: Notify
pages._doc: #1495 NEW CATEGORY: /notify/*, the obs.notify.* tools and the Telegram bridge. Data only: OpsMapFragment maps.hier_obs_notify.

sections.label: Observ
sections._doc: What the estate is doing. Today that is Health — the SuperApp's own page:c3/health, both tables with their counts in one view.

pages.label: Observability
pages._doc: #648 the SuperApp's Observability tab CARRIED WHOLE: C3StackFragment renders ui.sections[c3].stack_observability — the Index row, the FIVE feed cards (Analytics/github_run_stats, GHA/github_runs, Dagu/dagu_runs, GH Repos/github_commits, Gitea Repos/gitea_commits), the NTFY notification centre (stream=channels, last 5 per channel), and the More row.

pages.label: Dagu
pages._doc: #648 the SuperApp's page:c3/dagu — libs:ops DaguFragment, the native DAG list with per-row Run buttons and the Authelia-bearer login whose server URL pre-fills from ui.sections[c3].pages[dagu].dagu_default_server. The same fragment the Dagu feed card's rows and the More row target.

pages.label: WG mesh
pages._doc: #648 the SuperApp's page:wg/status — C3MeshFragment over the canonical wg-mesh/v1 snapshot (data/mesh.json), grouped by transport. It is the More row's 'WG mesh' target on the Observability stack, which is why it lives under this tab.

sections.label: Configs
sections._doc: This app's own settings, NOT in ui.bottom_nav: the top bar's Settings > Configs opens it (libs:bottomnav AppTopBar, ui.top_bar). #1443 Configs starts General | Perms | About (the fleet's shared pages of libs:ui-nav-bars, FleetConfigsPageFragment), then Build, this app's own card (everything it shows is baked by gradle).

pages.label: Plugins
pages._doc: #1495 NEW CATEGORY: the plugin.* tools of cloudy-c3-mcp (list, read, write, deploy of the Claude plugin files). Data only: OpsMapFragment maps.hier_plugins.

ui._doc_c3_ops: The SAME c3-infra-api the SuperApp's C3 pages read (its build.json::ui.c3_ops). This APK is a new FRONT over the existing engine, not a second back end, so the base URL is declared once here and OpsClient is the only file that names a route.
ui._doc_external_apps: #648 THE APPS TAB. Watchdog, Morpheus and WatchTower are ALREADY standalone fleet members with their own directories, build.json, ship workflow and applicationId — so this tab LAUNCHES them and declares no page of its own. This is the same extapp: idiom the SuperApp's ui.sections[c3] used for exactly these three, moved here with the section. A tile resolves its package against the device rather than assuming it is installed, so a missing app reads as 'not installed' instead of a tap that does nothing.
ui._doc_external_apps_no_label: THERE IS NO `label` HERE, AND THAT IS THE #351/#224 RULE, not an omission. An application has ONE name — the fleet name in its own build.json::name — and a label sitting beside a package is a SECOND statement of it that drifts; #224 is literally the commit that reverted a display name back to the fleet name, and aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-app-names-pattern.sh T4 fails the build on any object that names one of our packages next to a disagreeing label. The id IS the name and is what the tile shows. The owner's request named these three as 'Watchdog', 'Morpheus' and 'Watchtower'; the fleet spells them c3-watchdog / c3-morpheus / c3-watchtower, and the spelling shown is the fleet's — reported to the owner rather than settled by adding a private display name here.
ui._doc_topology: The Ops section's five topology views, declared once (owner table: view | grouping key | dominant metric | incident scenario). `missing` names what NO fleet endpoint provides today; the page prints it under the view instead of drawing a number nobody measured. `release` is the repository whose workflow runs the Release view reads (GitHub REST, unauthenticated, like the GHA feed).

views.metric: Up state per node; auth tier per edge
views.question: Which downstream causes 500s?

views.metric: Disk usage per VM; containers up per VM
views.question: Is there a noisy neighbour?

views.grouping: Fleet, VM, compose project, service, container
views.question: Did the latest commit apply, are replicas healthy?
missing: commit SHA the deployed state was applied from

views.grouping: WireGuard subnet, VM, Caddy route or firewall rule, container IP:port
views.metric: Routes and rules per VM, auth tier per route
views.question: Is a policy dropping packets?

views.grouping: Environment (VM), service version (image tag), last Ship runs
views.metric: Declared vs running image tag; last run conclusion
views.question: Did a fresh deploy regress?
missing: error rate before and after a deploy

apps_page._doc: THE Apps tab's Services and Tools pages (view-only). `tools` are the individual engines, each `source` a dotted path into cloud-infra's _cloud-data-consolidated.json (services.<name> | native.<name>); data/gen_infra_slice.py reads those paths and every host, zone, rule and port list from the export into data/infra_slice.json, so no host list is typed here. `services` are the composites: each names the tools it uses (a tool's 'used by' list is the inverse, derived) and the `views` it renders over the slice (InfraViews.kt has one renderer per view id; test-c3-shell.sh T9 diffs both ways). A tool's printed name is derived from its id (#351).

external_apps._doc: The phone's local web server (ac_cloud-c3-webserver, #687) is a cloud-c3 sub-app, so it launches from HERE beside the three siblings and not from the SuperApp's Cloud > Apps > Configs grid (aa_cloud-superapp/test/test-c3-family-apps.sh T2 fails if it goes back there). Still installed from the Store: its fleet row is untouched. No label (#351): the tile prints the id with the family prefix dropped.

ui._doc_pages: THE RULE (#648): a page appears here when its fragment exists, and not before. The SuperApp's five feed cards, its ntfy centre and its three container dashboards ARRIVED with the Observability/Topology stack pages above (C3StackFragment over ui.sections[c3].stack_*); Dagu and the WG mesh arrived as their own pages. The SuperApp page ids that have no fragment THERE either (reports, stack, workflows, vms, logs, gha — page_samples stubs) stay undeclared here, preserved only inside ui.sections[c3].pages; their More-row tiles dispatch an honest 'not shipped in this app'.
ui._doc_icons: An icon name here is a DRAWABLE name in res/drawable, resolved by getIdentifier at runtime (the ac_cloud-me contract). It is no longer a Compose vocabulary key: the shell is Views, because the pages this app hosts are the Fragments the SuperApp already had. A name with no drawable resolves to 0 and draws a blank square, so test-c3-shell.sh asserts every declared name has a file and every file is declared — in both directions.
ui._doc_tile_columns: How many tiles an index/dashboard row holds before wrapping — the SAME value the SuperApp bakes (ui.tile_columns), moved with the stacks that read it (IndexTiles.grid, the cloud_dashboard icon grids).
ui._doc_sections: #648 THE ENTIRE c3 declaration block of aa_cloud-superapp/build.json::ui.sections[id=c3], carried over VERBATIM — tabs, the visible AND hidden pages, stack_observability (the five feed cards + the NTFY centre + the Index/More rows) and stack_topology (the address cards + the three container dashboards), every _doc intact. THIS COPY IS WHAT THE APP RENDERS: app/build.gradle bakes stack_observability / stack_topology from HERE, and libs:ops reads pages[dagu].dagu_default_server from HERE (its consumer-wins lookup is ui.sections[id=c3]). The SuperApp's own copy stays where it was; this one is the independently editable duplicate the fleet's COPY rule asks for. Page ids that carry no fragment in the SuperApp either (reports, stack, workflows, vms, logs, gha land on its page_samples stub) are NOT declared as pages of this app's tabs — the #648 rule stands: a page is declared when its fragment exists — but their declarations are preserved here and their tiles in the two stacks dispatch an honest 'not shipped in this app' rather than a dead tap.
ui._doc_carried_c3: The SuperApp's c3 declaration block, carried VERBATIM (#648): its stack_topology / stack_observability ARE the Topology and Observ pages' bodies (C3StackFragment) and its `pages` keeps every SuperApp page id, shipped or not. It is a CARRIED DECLARATION, not navigation: the app's nav is ui.bottom_nav + ui.sections above, and a section id here (`c3`) is not a bar section.

carried_c3.label: C3
carried_c3._doc_parent: Back from the C3 tab strip ROOT lands on Cloud, not Home. navigateUpToParent() consults parent only when the back stack is empty, which is exactly the strip-root case — without this, that press fell through to goHome(). Distinct from the tab-restore fix in LauncherNavController (activeTabBySection), which governs returning from a SUBPAGE to the tab it was opened from.
carried_c3._doc_tabs: C3 IS its two halves, so it wears the same tab strip every other tabbed section wears (SectionTabsFragment + AppTabsStyle, driven purely by `tabs` + the visible `pages` below). Observability and Topology are the only two listed pages; the six detail pages under them are `hidden` — still routable as page:c3/<id>, and reached from the tile_row that leads each tab, exactly where they were reached from before. Two listed pages is also what makes this a strip rather than a rail: goSection only falls to SectionMenuFragment past SectionTabsFragment.MAX_PANES.

pages.label: Topology
pages._doc: What the cloud IS — the container/stack dashboard that used to be the whole of Cloud ▸ C3, carried down one level unchanged. Reports are NOT here any more: they are output rather than structure, so the reports tile now lives in stack_observability. page:c3/reports itself is unchanged and still routes the same way. FIRST tab: structure before behaviour, and it is also the landing page, because SectionTabsFragment.startIndex falls to the first page with a blank `action`. The `|` divider is unaffected — it is positioned by indexOfFirst { action.isNotBlank() }, which is still Watchdog at index 2 whichever way the two content tabs are ordered.

pages.label: Observability
pages._doc: What the cloud is DOING — GHA + Dagu workflow runs, the full Dagu workflow inventory, the reports the cloud produces, the workflow pages, and per-repo commit history. Reports moved here from Topology: Topology is what the fleet IS, and a report is output, not structure. A facet renders this section's own stack_observability; `facet` needs no `is_aggregator` on the section, only a stack_<page id> to read.

pages.label: Watchdog
pages._doc: A LAUNCH tab, not a content tab: it carries no facet and no fragment, only the same `action` grammar Configs' Keyboard entry uses, so tapping it dispatches extapp:c3-watchdog and the C3 strip stays where it was. That reuses launchExternalApp verbatim — the app opens when com.diegonmarcos.watchdog is installed, and when it is NOT the user is told so and the APK from ui.external_apps[id=c3-watchdog].install_apk_url is offered, instead of a tab that does nothing. is_action is what stops it being counted as a page anywhere a page means content.

pages.label: Morpheus
pages._doc: The second LAUNCH tab, identical in shape to Watchdog above: dispatches extapp:c3-morpheus (com.diegonmarcos.morpheus), falling back to installing ui.external_apps[id=c3-morpheus].install_apk_url. Morpheus shipped recently, so the not-installed path is the COMMON one here, not the edge case.

pages.label: WatchTower
pages._doc: The third LAUNCH tab, identical in shape to Watchdog and Morpheus above: no facet, no fragment, only an `action`, so tapping it dispatches extapp:c3-watchtower (com.diegonmarcos.watchtower) and the C3 strip stays where it was. Not installed -> the user is told so and ui.external_apps[id=c3-watchtower].install_apk_url is offered. is_action is what stops it being counted as a page anywhere a page means content. THE APP IS BRAND NEW, so the not-installed path is the ONLY path until the first ship run publishes, exactly as Morpheus's _doc records of its own first days.
pages._doc_index: INDEX 4, AFTER MORPHEUS, and the position is the requirement rather than a detail of it - the owner asked for it 'beside Morpheus'. stack_observability._doc:
ANALYTICS — the glance. Every other card on this page is a FEED: the latest N things that happened. This one is the only card that counts rather than lists, and that is exactly what the owner asked WatchTower to be, stated at card depth: over the last `limit` runs per repo, how many ran, what share of the FINISHED ones went green, and how long ago the last green was.

WHY THE DENOMINATOR IS 'FINISHED' AND NOT 'ALL'. A run still in progress carries an empty `conclusion`. Counting those as not-green makes the rate sag every time the fleet is mid-build, which is precisely when somebody opens this page. Queued and running are neither green nor failed — they are not yet anything. renderRunStatsFeed divides by the finished count and says 'no verdicts yet' rather than '0%' when that count is zero, because a rate with an empty denominator is not a rate.

SOURCE, NOT A NEW KIND. kind=feed with a sixth `source`, per this page's own long-standing instruction: a new integration is a new `when` arm in AggregatorStackFragment.renderFeed plus a client, never a new panel `kind`. It reads the SAME GitHubFeed.runs() the GHA card above reads, through the same 15-minute cache, so the two cards cost ONE fetch per repo between them and cannot disagree about a number.

THE REPO SET IS THIS ARRAY AND NOTHING ELSE, the same contract the GH Repos card documents. Deliberately the same three as the GHA card below (android/cloud/front) rather than ac_c3-watchtower's five: this is the glance and stays narrow, the app is the detail and carries the wider set. Adding a repo here is a data edit, never a Kotlin one.

OPENING THE FULL THING: the card's summary row targets extapp:c3-watchtower, so a tap hands off to the app through the SAME single dispatch chokepoint every other row uses (onTileClicked -> routeTarget -> launchExternalApp) — no seventh ad-hoc ACTION_VIEW site (#156), and the click still fires exactly once (#195). It is NOT in the More row below: More opens 'the full page behind a card' and its tiles are ordinary page: targets into HIDDEN c3 pages. There is no page:c3/analytics, and inventing one to have somewhere to point would add an un-wired stub page to satisfy a row.

THIS ARRAY IS THE REPO SET: AggregatorStackFragment.renderRepoCommitsFeed iterates Sections.StackPanel.repos and nothing else, so adding a repo is a data edit here, never a Kotlin edit. The list is every repo of the two families that GitHub actually answers 200 for, verified against api.github.com/repos/diegonmarcos/<name>. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, so nobody re-adds them: `cloud-android` and `cloud-unix` answer 301 and redirect to `cloud-u-android` and `cloud-infra-desktop` respectively — they are rename-aliases of repos already listed, and adding them would duplicate every commit; `cloud-mykonsole-dtk` answers 404, the upstream is gone and only the gitea mirror still remembers it; `front` (the ~30-project web monorepo) answers 404 too — it has no GitHub remote at all, and diegonmarcos.github.io is the published front site, which is why THAT is the front entry rather than `front`. Rate limit: this panel plus GHA share GitHub's 60-requests-per-hour anonymous quota, so GitHubFeed caches for 15 minutes, staggers the fan-out, and reports an exhausted quota as `rate limited` rather than as an empty repo. This SAME repo list (different `owner`) is reused verbatim by the Gitea Repos card below, so the two cards are directly comparable — same repos, two mirrors.

ui._doc_ntfy:
USER vs INFRA channel split for the ntfy registry. The channels are one flat list of snake_case topics upstream, so 'my notifications' and 'the cloud's notifications' arrived indistinguishable in one alphabetical wall. Scope is decided by the topic PREFIX, declared here rather than hardcoded in the fragment (FIRE RULE #6): a new prefix is a build.json edit. Anything unmatched counts as INFRA, so a channel can never silently vanish from the list — it lands in the cloud bucket and is visible enough to classify.

`channels` below IS the ntfy registry's own topics[] list — the source of truth is /home/appuser/git/cloud-u-containers/infra-obs_ntfy/src/build.json::topics (this app's clone lives at cloud-u-android, a SIBLING checkout to cloud-u-containers, not a `a_solutions` submodule of it — a path this comment previously got wrong). Verified 2026-09-06: every one of that registry's 23 topic names is present below; `cloud-sa-notifications` / `fleet_advisory` / `infra_mail-health` are the only extras, and they are legitimately NOT in that registry — they are this app's own advisory-scope channels (see `advisory_topic` below), published by a different mechanism than the fleet's ntfy topic list. There is no automated sync from that JSON into this one yet (the two live in different repos and this task's scope did not include building that pipeline); a topic added to the registry needs a matching manual edit here until one exists.
ui._doc_ntfy_copy: #648 VERBATIM copy of the SuperApp's ui.ntfy (labels, scopes, taxon, channels, poll origin) — the catalog the NTFY card in stack_observability resolves its channel list, labels and poll URL from (NtfyCatalog/NtfyScopes, moved with the card).

ntfy._doc_base_url: Origin for PROGRAMMATIC reads (the JSON poll API). This is ntfy itself on the WireGuard mesh. It is NOT rss.diegonmarcos.com: that hostname is the same container behind Caddy, whose only anonymous prefix is /feed* (infra-sec_caddy/src/caddyfile.nix::mkNtfyBlock, feed_auth="none"), and /feed* is served by the rss-gateway sidecar which publishes profiles.json, channels.json and <profile>.atom / c/<topic>.atom — it has no /<topic>/json route at all. Every other path on that host falls through to `handle { forward_auth authelia }` and answers 302 to the SSO portal, which is the 401 the Notify cards rendered. Measured anonymously from a mesh peer on 2026-09-09: /feed/channels.json 200, /feed/<topic>/json 404, /<topic>/json 302 -> auth.diegonmarcos.com, http://10.0.0.6:8090/<topic>/json 200 for all 26 channels below.
ntfy._doc_web_base_url: Origin for HUMAN links — the topic page a card opens in the in-app browser. The public hostname on purpose: a WebView carries the Authelia session cookie and satisfies the gate, which is the tier that exists for people.
ntfy._doc_poll_window: `since` for the channel cards, in a unit ntfy parses — s/m/h, a Unix timestamp, a message id or `all`. NEVER `d`: since=7d answers HTTP 400 {"code":40008}. Kept at a day rather than a week because health_resources alone replays 851 KB / 2101 messages over 24h and 3.6 MB over 168h, and a shade only ever shows the newest handful.

ntfy._doc_labels: Human titles, loosely mirrored from the fleet's own registry at cloud-u-containers/infra-obs_ntfy/src/build.json::topics[].desc (the source of truth) — reworded for length rather than copied verbatim. A raw snake_case topic is an address, not a name: 'sec_yara' tells you nothing about what arrives there, and a list of twenty-six of them is an inventory nobody reads. A topic with no entry here still renders — under its raw name — because a missing label must degrade to less readable, never to invisible.

labels.fleet_advisory: Fleet advisories · app is stuck, here is the fix

ntfy._doc_taxon: Section PREFIX per cloud publisher, in the same one-character vocabulary ui.phone_sections declares ("_" Sys, "@" Inboxes & AI, "." Data Apps, "=" Primary, ">" Media, "*" Health, "-"/"+" Services). The Notify tabs narrow phone groups by running PhoneAppClassifier over each package, but a cloud message carries no package — only an ntfy topic or an in-app producer name — so there is nothing to classify and this map is the classification. Without it every cloud publisher passed the taxonomy filter untouched and the SuperApp updater appeared on all six tabs, listed under Inboxes and under Data Apps as readily as under Sys. A key that is NOT declared here shows on the All tab only: a publisher nobody has categorised must not silently claim a category. Keys are matched against the group key, which is the topic for a channel and NotificationStore.source for the in-app feed.

Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Command and control for the whole cloud
about.description: Cloud C3 is the fleet's command-and-control surface as its own app, lifted out of the SuperApp's C3 section. Five tabs cover the cloud end to end: Infra (providers, VMs, storage, domains), Containers (topology, table, agents), Home, Ops (services, orchestration, network, releases) and Observ (health, Dagu, the WireGuard mesh). It exists so the owner can operate the cloud from the phone with the same data the desktop tools use, through the private mesh first and the signed-in public route as fallback.

screens.name: Containers
screens.what: Topology, the container table and agents.

screens.name: Observ
screens.what: Health, Dagu runs and the WireGuard mesh.

guide: Join the private mesh or sign in with Cloud Account.
Start on Home for what needs attention.
Use Containers to restart or inspect a service.
Check Observ for health history and the mesh.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It talks only to the fleet services listed below, over the private mesh first.

related.why: Signs in to the fleet and holds the tokens and secrets this app reads.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
